text:
Maria Chen: noticed a memory growth trend on Dedicated during long-context runs, looks like KV pages aren't being reclaimed consistently. Sam Ortiz: ugh, saw that too in the 32k chat load test yesterday. page count keeps climbing after ~10k tokens. Maria Chen: differences across deployments: Hosted is fine, Dedicated grows, Private (on-prem) is noisy depending on driver/hugepage settings. Lee Patel: could be allocator interaction (jemalloc vs system) + kernel madvise behavior on our configs. Anya Ivanov: also remember VPC MTU and NIC offload differences on cloud nodes — we saw subtle NUMA/page-migration before. OpsOnCall: any clear repro steps? I can spin up a dedicated replica. Maria Chen: simplest repro: run vokel/longctx-bench (we used the 16/32 batch mix), feed 8 sessions with 20k seq each, watch /proc/<pid>/maps and nvprof for GPU KV usage. Sam Ortiz: attached snippet of the monitoring we ran: ```
# summary
epoch 0: mem=14.2GB kv_pages=210k
epoch 50: mem=18.7GB kv_pages=275k
...
vmstat shows increases in pgmajfaults on Dedicated
``` Lee Patel: interestingly, kernel selected different page sizes on Dedicated nodes (no hugepages) whereas Hosted has transparent hugepages enabled. That affects fragmentation a lot. Anya Ivanov: on Private we saw a misconfiguration where cgroup memory.high triggered earlier leading to more evictions and then re-materialization churn. Maria Chen: profiling shows eviction spikes aligned with batch heuristics changes — when throughput optimizer switches to larger batch sizes we create more transient KV frames and eviction pressure increases. Sam Ortiz: can we try forcing batch cap to 8 and disable dynamic kernel fallback? Lee Patel: yes, try `runtime.config.batch.max_tokens=8` and `runtime.config.kernel.fallback=false` for a test. OpsOnCall: i'll deploy that to a dedicated canary. InfraBot: deploy started: canary/dedicated/kv-repro-2248 -> healthy. Anya Ivanov: also patch to jemalloc arena tuning helped on Private: lower per-thread arenas reduced fragmentation in our on-prem tests. Maria Chen: note — we saw page reclamation being delayed because some KV frames are pinned by GPU DMA; the driver on older on-prem cards doesn't unpin quickly when pages are freed. Lee Patel: that's the on-prem GPU nuance. For Hosted/Dedicated using newer drivers it's less pronounced. Sam Ortiz: after canary with batch cap=8 we saw mem plateau at ~15GB, no steady climb. Maria Chen: great, we should: 1) add the batch cap suggestion to Optimize rules for Dedicated, 2) add jemalloc arena recommendation for Private onprem guide, 3) investigate kernel tunables (transparent hugepage vs madvise) for Dedicated AMI. Anya Ivanov: i'll open a follow-up runbook PR with the jemalloc flags and a checklist for driver versions. OpsOnCall: also add alert for sustained kv_pages growth > 20% over 30m. Lee Patel: for longer term, runtime should prefer eviction-friendly kernel path when driver reports pinned pages. Maria Chen: Agreed — filing a runtime task to add a kernel-selection heuristic based on pinned page metrics. Sam Ortiz: thanks team, keep logs from the canary in #eng-runtime and tag me. Maria Chen: saved logs here: https://internal.redwood/logs/2248-kv-canary (link) :thumbsup:
